thread:
liz_support: FYI Acme reported a sudden p95 latency jump and a burst of 502s starting ~09:12 UTC after they switched to the new batch param in the SDK. They say ~20% of requests returned 502s, others timed out.
acme_infra_eng: Confirmed. We flipped batch_size=16 -> 64 in their client at 09:10. Saw error rate spike ~09:12.
liz_support: They hit us because they retried aggressively. Billing spike complaint incoming.
maya_eng: Possible hypothesis: larger batches increase memory/KV cache pressure causing worker rejection (502). Can you grab gateway logs and the worker `/metrics` around 09:05-09:20?
raj_sre: I pulled edge/gateway traces. Gateway returned 502 when upstream returned connection reset or closed during body streaming. Also some 504s from proxy timeouts. Correlation: high request sizes + longer queueing.
acme_infra_eng: Here's a snippet from their client config they pasted: `sdk.generate({ model: "rwd-13b", batch_size: 64, max_tokens: 1024 })` and they have retries set to 5 with no backoff.
liz_support: Customer wants a mitigation ASAP and explanation for billing.
maya_eng: Quick mitigation: suggest client rollback to batch_size=16 and reduce retries/backoff. Also throttle their requests at our edge using per-tenant concurrency cap.
raj_sre: I'm adding a soft limit rule for their tenant (t-acme) to cap concurrent inflight to 8 for next 30m. Will monitor. 
oncall_bot: [oncall] Created incident INC-2028: tenant t-acme inflight surge causing 502s. Pager suppressed.
kevin_account: I'll draft a temporary customer note: "We're investigating elevated error rate after you increased client batch size. Please revert to previous batch size for immediate mitigation. We're applying a temporary concurrency cap to stabilize service." Any objections?
maya_eng: No objection. Also adding a temporary fallback policy in the router: if a worker rejects due to memory pressure, route to smaller model variant (rwd-13b-quant) as fallback. Rolling this change to canary now.
raj_sre: Canary applied to 10% of traffic for t-acme. Initial telemetry shows error rate dropping ~60% within 2 mins. p95 latency back down ~300ms -> 120ms.
acme_infra_eng: Confirmed on our side that errors dropped after rollback to batch_size=16 and you applying the cap. Thanks.
liz_support: Customer notified. They asked if this could cause duplicate billing due to retries.
maya_eng: If they retried and server returned 502, some requests may have completed upstream before client saw the error. We need to check request IDs and billing logs to determine duplicates.
raj_sre: I exported a sample of request IDs for 09:10-09:20 and matched backend completion events. ~8% of failed requests actually completed at worker side before connection close. We'll flag those for billing review.
kevin_account: I'll pause billing for t-acme for the window 09:10-09:20 pending investigation.
liz_support: Good. Any permanent mitigation suggestions?
maya_eng: Developer guidance: (1) avoid batch_size jumps without staged rollout, (2) SDK should use exponential backoff with jitter and idempotency keys for large requests, (3) server-side: softer rejection with `Retry-After` headers and a better 5xx -> 429 graceful degrade path so clients don't assume immediate success and retry blind.
raj_sre: We should also add telemetry to detect sudden per-tenant increase in average request token count and auto-enforce a progressive concurrency reduction rather than blunt caps. I'll open a follow-up ticket.
liz_support: Action items: kevin pause billing (done), raj cap + telemetry (done + in progress), maya fallback routing + canary (done), ask customer to revert batch and SDK backoff (sent).
acme_infra_eng: Received. We'll keep batch_size at 16 and add backoff. Will follow up after billing update.
liz_support: Closing thread for now, keeping incident open for billing reconciliation. :thumbsup:
